form.title: New Patient Intake Form
form.subtitle: Please print clearly. Use black or blue ink. Please do not write 'see chart.'
form.disclaimer: Fiction. LLM-generated parody of a front-desk paper form. Not a real patient, not a real form, not medical advice.
form.completed_in: the waiting room, on a clipboard with a pen chained to it

sections.title: Section 1 — Who Is Actually Holding The Pen

questions.label: Filled out by (if not the patient)
questions.answer: Olive Turnip (wife). He says I'm better at forms. He is correct.
questions.front_desk_note: Patient present, alert, oriented, and pointing at his wife.

questions.label: Today's date
questions.front_desk_note: Correct on the first try. Rare.

questions.label: Patient name
questions.front_desk_note: Spelled the same on all nine visits. A miracle.

questions.label: Date of birth
questions.front_desk_note: He is 61 and would like that known in a specific tone of voice.

questions.label: Address
questions.answer: 12 Garden Row. The one with the fence dispute.
questions.front_desk_note: Unprompted fence mention #1.

questions.label: Phone
questions.front_desk_note: This is Olive's phone. Fig's phone is on the kitchen counter, on silent, at 4%.

questions.label: Insurance
questions.front_desk_note: Says 'my work.' Wife is filling this out. Card is under HER employer. Billing will find out in eleven days.

questions.label: Member ID
questions.front_desk_note: Card is in the other purse. The card is always in the other purse.

questions.label: Emergency contact (name, relationship, phone)
questions.front_desk_note: Same number as the patient. In an emergency, we will be calling the person sitting next to him.

questions.label: Reason for visit (please be specific)
questions.front_desk_note: Eighteen months, nine visits, five doctors, one word.

questions.label: How long has this been going on?
questions.answer: Since the knee. Or before the knee. Olive says before.
questions.front_desk_note: Olive is right. It was before the knee.

questions.label: Rate your pain from 0 to 10
questions.verbatim: 8, but that's a normal 8. Not an 8 8.
questions.front_desk_note: Has been between 6 and 9 on every visit since March 2025. The number has stopped meaning anything to everyone involved.

questions.label: What makes it better?
questions.front_desk_note: Mutually exclusive. Left as written.

questions.label: What makes it worse?
questions.front_desk_note: Unprompted fence mention #2. Possibly the only honest answer on this form.

sections.title: Section 3 — Current Medications (include over-the-counter, vitamins, eye drops, inhalers)

questions.label: List all medications, dose, and how often
questions.answer: metformin, the nerve pill, meloxicam, tylenol
questions.front_desk_note: Four items listed. Chart says five. One of the five he stopped months ago and did not mention. That one is the antidepressant.

questions.label: (Not a question on the form. Somebody should add it.)
questions.answer: All of them. One bottle. He shakes it and takes what comes out.
questions.front_desk_note: There is a photo. The photo is worse than the sentence.

questions.label: Do you take your medications as prescribed?
questions.actual_answer: Skips the nerve pill when he has anything to do that day, because it makes him foggy. Takes the tylenol 'whenever.' Finished the muscle relaxer sometime in 2025 and nobody refilled it, which everyone is treating as a clinical decision.
questions.front_desk_note: The checkbox and the truth are not on speaking terms.

questions.label: Allergies
questions.front_desk_note: Chart, in red, at the top, in a font designed to be unmissable: CODEINE — NAUSEA.

questions.label: Past conditions (check all that apply)
questions.front_desk_note: 'Depression / anxiety' is one row below 'Diabetes' and was not ticked. He is on a medication for it. Was on. Was.

questions.label: Past surgeries (procedure and year)
questions.front_desk_note: Procedure: partially provided. Year: 2019, available in the chart, four feet away, on a screen.

questions.label: Family history (parents, siblings, children: cancer, diabetes, heart disease, stroke, glaucoma)
questions.front_desk_note: Two words. A whole man, summarized.

questions.label: Tobacco
questions.front_desk_note: Quit when? The line is RIGHT THERE. It is a line specifically for that.

questions.label: Alcohol
questions.front_desk_note: Three options. Invented a fourth. 'Some' is doing a lot of work here.

questions.label: Recreational drugs
questions.front_desk_note: The one question on this form that was answered exactly as designed. Framed it.

questions.label: (Not asked. Should be.)
questions.answer: Not sleeping. Hasn't been, for a long time. Nobody has asked, because there is no box.
questions.front_desk_note: The most clinically useful sentence in this document is in a section that does not exist.

questions.label: Signature (if not the patient, relationship: ________)
questions.front_desk_note: Signed by the wife. Who wrote it. Who will do the talking. Who has, at some point in the last eighteen months, quietly become the patient's interface layer.

contradictions: Insurance 'through my work' vs. spouse's employer plan
Medication list omits sertraline, which he stopped months ago without telling anyone
scoring.recommended_next_step: Stop reading the form. Ask him about the fence. He will tell you everything else on the way there.

the_joke: Every answer on this form is technically a valid response to the question printed above it. The form is working perfectly. That is the problem.
